sections.chapter_title: Controller area network with flexible data rate (FDCAN)
sections.section_title: FDCAN data bit timing and prescaler register (FDCAN_DBTP)
sections.text_helper: Section 71.5.3 "FDCAN data bit timing and prescaler register (FDCAN_DBTP)" in chapter 71 (Controller area network with flexible data rate (FDCAN)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 3681.
sections.section_content:
Address offset: 0x000C
Reset value: 0x0000 0A33
This register is dedicated to data bit timing phase and only writable if bits
FDCAN_CCCR.CCE and FDCAN_CCCR.INIT are set. The CAN time quantum may be
programmed in the range from 1 to 32 FDCAN clock periods. tq = (DBRP + 1) FDCAN clock
periods.
DTSEG1 is the sum of Prop_Seg and Phase_Seg1. DTSEG2 is Phase_Seg2. Therefore the
length of the bit time is (DTSEG1 + DTSEG2 + 3) tq for programmed values, or
(Sync_Seg+Prop_Seg+Phase_Seg1+Phase_Seg2) tq for functional values.
The information processing time (IPT) is zero, meaning the data for the next bit is available
at the first clock edge after the sample point.
Bits 31:24 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bit 23 TDC: Transceiver delay compensation
0: Transceiver delay compensation disabled
1: Transceiver delay compensation enabled
Bits 22:21 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bits 20:16 DBRP[4:0]: Data bitrate prescaler
The value by which the oscillator frequency is divided to generate the bit time quanta. The bit time is
built up from a multiple of these quanta. Valid values for the baudrate prescaler are 0 to 31. The
hardware interpreters this value as the programmed value plus 1.
Bits 15:13 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
Bits 12:8 DTSEG1[4:0]: Data time segment before sample point
Valid values are 0 to 31. The value used by the hardware is the one programmed, incremented by 1,
that is, tBS1 = (DTSEG1 + 1) x tq.
Bits 7:4 DTSEG2[3:0]: Data time segment after sample point
Valid values are 0 to 15. The value used by the hardware is the one programmed, incremented by 1,
that is, tBS2 = (DTSEG2 + 1) x tq.
Bits 3:0 DSJW[3:0]: Synchronization jump width
Valid values are 0 to 15. The value used by the hardware is the one programmed, incremented by 1,
that is, tSJW = (DSJW + 1) x tq.
Note: With a CAN kernel clock of 8 MHz, the reset value of 0x00000A33 configures the FDCAN
for a bit rate of 500 kbit/s.
Note: The data phase bit rate must be higher than or equal to the nominal bit rate.
